correctness.rationale: From CDF G=(E/D)^n with mass (1-p)^n and density n p alpha f E^(n-1)/D^(n+1), the LR derivative cancels f and has sign H(s)=(n−1)(beta(1−q)−alpha(1−p))−(n+1)(beta−alpha)P(s), P=(Ea Eb)/(Da Db), strictly decreasing from 1 to (1−p)(1−q). For beta>=alpha, maximum H is at s=1 and atom inequality beta p(1−q)<=alpha q(1−p) implies H<=0; for beta<alpha, maximum at s=0 and H(0)<=0 is exactly (n−1)(beta q−alpha p)>=2(alpha−beta), which forces strict atom condition. Conversely violating the max/atom condition violates LR. Equality, beta=alpha, n=1, tails and zero atom are covered. Independently derived symbolic identities and 10,800 exact rational parameter checks passed; finite tests are ancillary, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 primary PO shock-model paper explicitly names LR comparison as a motivated open direction. The submitted all-parameter iff answers this natural strong-order problem for a broad homogeneous class, including the necessary atom-at-zero jump. Its sharp integer threshold when severity odds decrease but claim occurrence increases is a genuinely informative design tradeoff, not an arbitrary n=5 numerical lookup or a restatement of a known table. The work deliberately does not claim heterogeneous, unequal-size, dependent or varying-baseline extensions.
